newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian priest punished for drug lord's surrender.
newsitem.headline: Colombian priest punished for drug lord's surrender.

text.p: A Colombian Roman Catholic priest said on Thursday he had been officially chastised for helping to arrange the surrender of the last Cali cartel drug kingpin still at large.

"This is extremely regrettable," the priest, Raul Echeverry, told the Caracol radio network. He said he had been ordered to leave the archdiocese of Cali and return to his native Antioquia province immediately because he had placed the church at the service of "the mafia and drug trafficking."

He served as a go-between in last Sunday's surrender to police of Helmer "El Pacho" Herrera, No. 3 leader of the Cali cartel and the target of a manhunt for more than a year. The surrender took place in Echeverry's church in Yumbo, an industrial centre on the outskirts of the southwestern city that gave the infamous Cali drug organisation its name.

"The archbishop told me that I shouldn't have done what I did without telling him about it first," Echeverry said of the reason for his expulsion from Cali. "I told him that he had not been chosen, that the decision was made by the people involved in arranging the surrender, and that it was something I had to do as a priest," he said.
